title: حِكَايَةُ الْعَاشِقِ وَالْمَعْشُوقِ
titleEn: The Lover and the Beloved, continued
part: Night 109 · The Lover and the Beloved, continued
source: William Hay Macnaghten, ed., The Alif Laila, or Book of the Thousand Nights and One Night, vol. 1, Calcutta 1839 (“Calcutta II”), printed pp. 558–560 (Night 109, continuing directly from nights-108), transcribed from the 300 ppi scan (archive.org aliflailaorbooko01macn) by the editors' own transcription. The edition prints the prose essentially unpointed: ALL VOCALIZATION (tashkīl) IS EDITORIAL — ours, not the edition's — and the alphabet button strips it back to the bare rasm as Macnaghten prints it, except where a clear misprint has been corrected (each is noted). Romanization is simplified IJMES. Spelling, including the edition’s Middle Arabic forms, is preserved; clear misprints are corrected in the text, and the note on each gives the print’s reading. Obscure or doubtful forms are kept as printed, vocalized by evident sense and flagged in the notes. Read-aloud audio is a Modern Standard Arabic reading of this vocalised text, synthesized by machine, with word-by-word timing generated the same way.
about: Night 109 continues the story that the vizier Dandān tells within the tale of King ʿUmar ibn al-Nuʿmān, the story of the lover, the beloved and the go-between. The vizier brings Zahrshāh's daughter home, and Sulaymān Shāh sends his troops out with banners to meet her; a crier calls every woman in the city out to greet the bride, and the litter is carried to the palace to drums, trumpets and the display of lances. That night the marriage is consummated, and the queen conceives. Nine months later she bears a son, greeted with a short poem in praise of the future warrior, and he is named Tāj al-Mulūk Khārān. He is schooled in writing, philosophy and letters, then in horsemanship, and by fourteen everyone who sees him is captivated. As with every printed edition of the Nights, this one belongs to the late Egyptian recension (ZER) — an eighteenth-century expansion padded out to a literal 1001 nights; no printed edition is a medieval text, and Macnaghten regularised the language here and there, so some Middle Arabic texture is a nineteenth-century retrofit.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا كَانَتِ اللَّيْلَةُ التَّاسِعَةُ بَعْدَ الْمِائَةِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā kānati al-laylatu al-tāsiʿatu baʿda al-miʾati
sentences.l: And when it was the night, the ninth after the hundred,
sentences.i: And when it was the hundred and ninth night,

sentences.t: قَالَتْ بَلَغَنِي أَيُّهَا الْمَلِكُ السَّعِيدُ أَنَّ الْوَزِيرَ تَوَجَّهَ بِا بْنَةِ الْمَلِكِ وَسَارَ وَلَمْ يَزَلْ يَطْوِى الْمَرَاحِلَ وَالْقِفَارَ وَيُجِدُّ السَّيْرَ فِى اللَّيْلِ وَالنَّهَارِ حَتَّى بَقِيَ بَيْنَهُ وَبَيْنَ بِلَادِهِ ثَلٰثَةُ أَيَّامٍ
sentences.tr: qālat balaghanī ayyuhā al-maliku al-saʿīdu anna al-wazīra tawajjaha bi-ibnati al-maliki wa-sāra wa-lam yazal yaṭwī al-marāḥila wa-al-qifāra wa-yujiddu al-sayra fī al-layli wa-al-nahāri ḥattā baqiya baynahu wa-bayna bilādihi thalāthatu ayyāmin
sentences.l: She said: It has reached me, O king the happy, that the vizier set-out with the daughter of the king and journeyed, and did not cease folding-up the stages and the wastes and pressing the going in the night and the day, until there remained between him and his lands three days.
sentences.i: She said: It has reached me, O fortunate king, that the vizier set out with the king's daughter and travelled on, stage after stage and desert after desert, pressing on by night and by day, until only three days lay between him and his own country.
sentences.n: Shahrazād takes up the night by repeating the last sentence of the one before. The print again splits بابنة, “with the daughter”, across a space (با بنة). bi-, “with”: tawajjaha bi- is “set out with, escort”. al-qifār and al-nahār rhyme.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ أَرْسَلَ إِلَى الْمَلِكِ سُلَيْمَانَ شَاهْ مَنْ يُخْبِرُهُ بِقُدُومِ الْعَرُوسَةِ فَأَسْرَعَ الرَّسُولُ بِالسَّيْرِ حَتَّى وَصَلَ إِلَى الْمَلِكِ وَأَخْبَرَهُ بِقُدُومِ الْعَرُوسَةِ
sentences.tr: thumma arsala ilā al-maliki sulaymāna shāh man yukhbiruhu bi-qudūmi al-ʿarūsati fa-asraʿa al-rasūlu bi-al-sayri ḥattā waṣala ilā al-maliki wa-akhbarahu bi-qudūmi al-ʿarūsati
sentences.l: Then he sent to King Sulaymān Shāh one-who would inform him of the coming of the bride; and the messenger hastened in the going until he reached the king and informed him of the coming of the bride.
sentences.i: Then he sent a man ahead to tell King Sulaymān Shāh that the bride was coming. The messenger rode hard until he reached the king and gave him the news of the bride's approach.
sentences.n: ʿarūsa is the everyday form of Classical ʿarūs, “bride”. bi-, “of”: akhbara bi- is “inform of”, the verb choosing the preposition; in asraʿa bi-al-sayr, “hasten in the going”, it marks what is hurried.

sentences.t: فَفَرِحَ الْمَلِكُ سُلَيْمَانُ شَاهْ وَخَلَعَ عَلَى الرَّسُولِ وَأَمَرَ عَسَاكِرَهُ أَنْ يَخْرُجُوا فِي مَوْكِبٍ عَظِيمٍ إِلَى مُلَاقَاةِ الْعَرُوسَةِ وَمَنْ مَعَهَا بِالتَّكْرِيمِ وَأَنْ يَكُونُوا فِي أَحْسَنِ الْبَهَجَاتِ وَأَنْ يَنْشُرُوا عَلَى رُؤُسِهِمُ الرَّايَاتِ فَامْتَثَلُوا أَمْرَهُ
sentences.tr: fa-fariḥa al-maliku sulaymānu shāh wa-khalaʿa ʿalā al-rasūli wa-amara ʿasākirahu an yakhrujū fī mawkibin ʿaẓīmin ilā mulāqāti al-ʿarūsati wa-man maʿahā bi-al-takrīmi wa-an yakūnū fī aḥsani al-bahajāti wa-an yanshurū ʿalā ruʾūsihimu al-rāyāti fa-imtathalū amrahu
sentences.l: And King Sulaymān Shāh rejoiced, and robed upon the messenger, and ordered his troops that they go-out in a great procession to the meeting of the bride and who-was with her, with honouring, and that they be in the finest of the splendours, and that they spread over their heads the banners; and they complied-with his order.
sentences.i: King Sulaymān Shāh was overjoyed. He gave the messenger a robe of honour and ordered his troops to ride out in a great procession and meet the bride and her company with every honour, to be at their most splendid, and to unfurl the banners over their heads; and they did as he commanded.
sentences.n: The print has تكونوا, “that you be”, a misprint for يكونوا, “that they be”, corrected here; the verbs on either side of it are third person. khalaʿa ʿalā, “to robe someone”, is to reward him with a robe of honour. bi-, “with”: the manner of the welcome.

sentences.t: وَنَادَى مُنَادٍ فِي الْمَدِينَةِ أَنَّهُ لَا تَبْقَى بِنْتٌ مُخَدَّرَةٌ وَلَا حُرَّةٌ مُوَقَّرَةٌ وَلَا عَجُوزٌ مُكَسَّرَةٌ إِلَّا وَتَخْرُجُ إِلَي لِقَاءِ الْعَرُوسَةِ فَخَرَجُوا جَمِيعًا إِلَى لِقَائِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-nādā munādin fī al-madīnati annahu lā tabqā bintun mukhaddaratun wa-lā ḥurratun muwaqqaratun wa-lā ʿajūzun mukassaratun illā wa-takhruju ilā liqāʾi al-ʿarūsati fa-kharajū jamīʿan ilā liqāʾihā
sentences.l: And a crier cried in the city that there should not remain a girl curtained, nor a free-woman honoured, nor an old-woman broken, but that she go-out to the meeting of the bride; and they went-out all to her meeting.
sentences.i: A crier went through the city proclaiming that no girl kept behind the curtain, no freeborn lady of standing and no old woman bent with age was to stay at home: every one of them was to go out to meet the bride. And they all went out to meet her.
sentences.n: The proclamation is rhymed prose: mukhaddara, muwaqqara, mukassara — the secluded daughter, the honoured lady, the broken-down old woman. The print writes إلى here with a dotted yāʾ, الي, as it sometimes does.

sentences.t: وَسَعَتْ كُبَرَاؤُهُمْ فِي خِدْمَتِهَا وَاتَّفَقُوا عَلَى أَنْ يَتَوَجَّهُوا بِهَا فِي اللَّيْلِ إِلَى قَصْرِ الْمَلِكِ
sentences.tr: wa-saʿat kubarāʾuhum fī khidmatihā wa-ittafaqū ʿalā an yatawajjahū bihā fī al-layli ilā qaṣri al-maliki
sentences.l: And their great-ones strove in her service, and they agreed on that they would go with her in the night to the palace of the king.
sentences.i: Their great men busied themselves in her service, and they agreed to bring her to the king's palace by night.
sentences.n: bihā: bi-, “with”: tawajjaha bi- is “set out with, conduct”, as above.

sentences.t: وَاتَّفَقَ أَرْبَابُ الدَّوْلَةِ عَلَى أَنْ يُزَيِّنُوا الطَّرِيقَ وَأَنْ يَقِفُوا حَتَّى تَمُرَّ بِهِمُ الْعَرُوسَةُ وَالْخُدَّامُ قُدَّامَهَا وَالْجَوَارِي بَيْنَ يَدَيْهَا وَعَلَيْهَا الْخِلْعَةُ الَّتِي أَعْطَاهَا لَهَا أَبُوهَا
sentences.tr: wa-ittafaqa arbābu al-dawlati ʿalā an yuzayyinū al-ṭarīqa wa-an yaqifū ḥattā tamurra bihimu al-ʿarūsatu wa-al-khuddāmu quddāmahā wa-al-jawārī bayna yadayhā wa-ʿalayhā al-khilʿatu allatī aʿṭāhā lahā abūhā
sentences.l: And the lords of the state agreed on that they adorn the road and that they stand until the bride should pass by them, and the servants in-front-of her and the slave-girls between her hands, and upon her the robe which her father had given it to her.
sentences.i: The lords of the realm agreed to deck out the road and to stand along it until the bride passed, her servants walking before her and her slave girls in attendance, and she wearing the robe her father had given her.
sentences.n: The print has وانفق, “and spent”, a misprint for واتفق, “and agreed”, corrected here; the sentence before has اتفقوا in the same sense. bihim: marra bi- is “pass by”, the verb choosing the preposition. bayna yadayhā, “between her hands”, means “in attendance on her”. aʿṭāhā lahā, “gave it to her”, with li- for the receiver, is an everyday turn where Classical Arabic would say aʿṭāhā iyyāhā.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَقْبَلَتْ أَحَاطَ بِهَا الْعَسْكَرُ ذَاتَ الْيَمِينِ وَذَاتَ الشِّمَالِ وَلَمْ تَزَلِ الْمِحَفَّةُ سَائِرَةً بِهَا إِلَى أَنْ قَرُبَتْ مِنَ الْقَصْرِ وَلَمْ يَبْقَ أَحَدٌ إِلَّا وَقَدْ خَرَجَ لِيَتَفَرَّجَ عَلَيْهَا
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aqbalat aḥāṭa bihā al-ʿaskaru dhāta al-yamīni wa-dhāta al-shimāli wa-lam tazali al-miḥaffatu sāʾiratan bihā ilā an qarubat mina al-qaṣri wa-lam yabqa aḥadun illā wa-qad kharaja li-yatafarraja ʿalayhā
sentences.l: And when she drew-near, the army surrounded her on the side of the right and the side of the left, and the litter did not cease going with her until it came-near to the palace; and there did not remain anyone but he had gone-out to look-on at her.
sentences.i: As she approached, the troops closed round her to right and left, and the litter bore her on until it neared the palace; and there was no one left who had not come out to gaze at her.
sentences.n: aḥāṭa bi- is “surround”, the verb choosing the preposition; in sāʾiratan bihā, bi- is “with, carrying”. li-, “in order to”: li-yatafarraja, “to look on”; tafarraja ʿalā is the everyday “watch, enjoy the sight of”.

sentences.t: وَصَارَتِ الطُّبُولُ ضَارِبَةً وَالرِّمَاحُ لَاعِبَةً وَالْبُوقَاتُ صَائِحَةً وَرَوَائِحُ الطِّيبِ فَائِحَةً وَالرَّايَاتُ خَافِقَةً وَالْخَيْلُ مُتَسَابِقَةً حَتَّى وَصَلُوا إِلَى بَابِ الْقَصْرِ
sentences.tr: wa-ṣārati al-ṭubūlu ḍāribatan wa-al-rimāḥu lāʿibatan wa-al-būqātu ṣāʾiḥatan wa-rawāʾiḥu al-ṭībi fāʾiḥatan wa-al-rāyātu khāfiqatan wa-al-khaylu mutasābiqatan ḥattā waṣalū ilā bābi al-qaṣri
sentences.l: And the drums became beating, and the lances playing, and the trumpets crying, and the scents of the perfume wafting, and the banners fluttering, and the horses racing-one-another, until they reached the door of the palace.
sentences.i: The drums beat, the lances played, the trumpets blared, the scent of perfume drifted on the air, the banners fluttered and the horses raced one another, until they came to the palace gate.
sentences.n: Another run of rhymed prose: ḍāriba, lāʿiba, ṣāʾiḥa, fāʾiḥa, khāfiqa, mutasābiqa. Lances “playing” are lances wielded in display, a mock combat in the bride's honour. būqāt, “trumpets”, is a plural of būq beside the more usual abwāq.

sentences.t: وَتَقَدَّمَتِ الْغِلْمَانُ بِالْمِحَفَّةِ إِلَى بَابِ السِّرِّ فَأَضَاءَ الْمَكَانُ بِبَهْجَتِهَا وَأَشْرَقَتْ جِهَاتُهُ بِحُلِيِّ زِينَتِهَا
sentences.tr: wa-taqaddamati al-ghilmānu bi-al-miḥaffati ilā bābi al-sirri fa-aḍāʾa al-makānu bi-bahjatihā wa-ashraqat jihātuhu bi-ḥuliyyi zīnatihā
sentences.l: And the pages went-forward with the litter to the door of the secret; and the place shone with her splendour, and its sides gleamed with the jewels of her adornment.
sentences.i: The pages carried the litter forward to the private gate, and the whole place was lit by her beauty, every corner of it glittering with the jewels she wore.
sentences.n: The print has فاضاو, a misprint for فاضاء, “and (it) shone”, corrected here. bāb al-sirr, “the door of the secret”, is the private gate of the palace. bi-, “with”: the litter carried forward; then, twice, the cause of the shining. bahjatihā and zīnatihā rhyme.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا أَقْبَلَ اللَّيْلُ فَتَحَ الْخُدَّامُ أَبْوَابَ السُّرَادِقِ وَوَقَفُوا وَهُمْ مُحْتَاطُونَ بِالْبَابِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā aqbala al-laylu fataḥa al-khuddāmu abwāba al-surādiqi wa-waqafū wa-hum muḥtāṭūna bi-al-bābi
sentences.l: And when the night came-on, the servants opened the doors of the pavilion and stood, while they (were) surrounding the door.
sentences.i: When night came on, the servants opened the doors of the pavilion and took their stand around the entrance.
sentences.n: surādiq is a great tent or pavilion; here the hung chamber prepared for the bride. muḥtāṭūna bi-, “surrounding”, from iḥtāṭa bi-, the verb choosing the preposition.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ جَاءَتِ الْعَرُوسَةُ وَهِيَ بَيْنَ الْجَوَارِي كَالْقَمَرِ بَيْنَ النُّجُومِ أَوِ الدُّرَّةِ الْفَرِيدَةِ بَيْنَ اللُّؤْلُؤِ الْمَنْظُومِ
sentences.tr: thumma jāʾati al-ʿarūsatu wa-hiya bayna al-jawārī ka-al-qamari bayna al-nujūmi awi al-durrati al-farīdati bayna al-luʾluʾi al-manẓūmi
sentences.l: Then the bride came, and she (was) among the slave-girls like the moon among the stars, or the pearl unique among the pearls strung.
sentences.i: Then the bride came in among her slave girls like the moon among the stars, or a matchless pearl among pearls on a string.
sentences.n: ka-, “like”: the comparison. al-durra al-farīda is the single great pearl at the centre of a necklace, al-luʾluʾ al-manẓūm the strung pearls around it. al-nujūm and al-manẓūm rhyme.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ دَخَلَتِ الْمَقْصُورَةَ وَقَدْ نَصَبُوا لَهَا سَرِيرًا مِنَ الْمَرْمَرِ مُرَصَّعًا بِالدُّرِّ وَالْجَوْهَرِ فَجَلَسَتْ عَلَيْهِ وَدَخَلَ عَلَيْهَا الْمَلِكُ وَأَوْقَعَ اللَّهُ مَحَبَّتَهَا فِي قَلْبِهِ
sentences.tr: thumma dakhalati al-maqṣūrata wa-qad naṣabū lahā sarīran mina al-marmari muraṣṣaʿan bi-al-durri wa-al-jawhari fa-jalasat ʿalayhi wa-dakhala ʿalayhā al-maliku wa-awqaʿa allāhu maḥabbatahā fī qalbihi
sentences.l: Then she entered the chamber, and they had set-up for her a couch of the marble, inlaid with the pearls and the jewels, and she sat on it. And the king went-in to her, and God cast the love of her into his heart,
sentences.i: Then she entered the inner chamber, where they had set up for her a couch of marble inlaid with pearls and jewels, and she sat down upon it. The king went in to her, and God put love for her into his heart;
sentences.n: maqṣūra is a private, closed-off room. bi-, “with”: what the couch is inlaid with. dakhala ʿalā, “go in to”, is also the phrase for the wedding night.

sentences.t: فَأَزَالَ بَكَارَتَهَا وَزَالَ مَا كَانَ عِنْدَهُ مِنَ الْقَلَقِ وَالْقَهْرِ وَأَقَامَ عِنْدَهَا نَحْوَ شَهْرٍ فَعَلِقَتْ مِنْهُ فِي أَوَّلِ لَيْلَةٍ
sentences.tr: fa-azāla bakāratahā wa-zāla mā kāna ʿindahu mina al-qalaqi wa-al-qahri wa-aqāma ʿindahā naḥwa shahrin fa-ʿaliqat minhu fī awwali laylatin
sentences.l: and he removed her virginity, and there went-away what had been with him of the restlessness and the vexation; and he stayed with her about a month, and she conceived by him in the first night.
sentences.i: he took her maidenhead, and all the restlessness and frustration he had suffered fell away from him. He stayed with her for about a month; and she had conceived by him on the very first night.
sentences.n: The play is on azāla, “he removed”, and zāla, “it went away”, from the same root. ʿaliqat, “she conceived”, is literally “she caught, clung”.

sentences.t: وَبَعْدَ تَمَامِ الشَّهْرِ خَرَجَ وَجَلَسَ عَلَى سَرِيرِ مَمْلَكَتِهِ وَعَدَلَ فِي رَعِيَّتِهِ إِلَى أَنْ وَفَتْ أَشْهُرُهَا
sentences.tr: wa-baʿda tamāmi al-shahri kharaja wa-jalasa ʿalā sarīri mamlakatihi wa-ʿadala fī raʿiyyatihi ilā an wafat ashhuruhā
sentences.l: And after the completion of the month he went-out and sat on the throne of his kingdom and did-justice among his subjects, until her months were-fulfilled.
sentences.i: When the month was over he came out, took his seat on the throne of his kingdom and ruled his subjects justly, until her months were fulfilled.
sentences.n: sarīr is both “couch”, as for the bride's marble couch above, and “throne”.

sentences.t: وَفِي آخِرِ لَيْلَةٍ مِنَ الشَّهْرِ التَّاسِعِ جَاءَهَا الْمَخَاضُ عِنْدَ السَّحَرِ فَجَلَسَتْ عَلَى كُرْسِيِّ الطَّلْقِ وَهَوَّنَ اللَّهُ عَلَيْهَا الْوِلَادَةَ فَوَضَعَتْ غُلَامًا ذَكَرًا تَلُوحُ عَلَيْهِ عَلَامَاتُ السَّعَادَةِ
sentences.tr: wa-fī ākhiri laylatin mina al-shahri al-tāsiʿi jāʾahā al-makhāḍu ʿinda al-saḥari fa-jalasat ʿalā kursiyyi al-ṭalqi wa-hawwana allāhu ʿalayhā al-wilādata fa-waḍaʿat ghulāman dhakaran talūḥu ʿalayhi ʿalāmātu al-saʿādati
sentences.l: And in the last night of the month the ninth, the labour came to her at the before-dawn; and she sat on the chair of the birth-pangs, and God made-easy for her the birth, and she bore a boy, a male, on whom gleamed the signs of the good-fortune.
sentences.i: On the last night of the ninth month her labour came upon her just before dawn. She sat on the birthing chair, God made the delivery easy for her, and she gave birth to a son on whom the signs of good fortune shone.
sentences.n: kursī al-ṭalq, “the chair of labour”, is the birthing stool. ghulāman dhakaran, “a boy, a male”, doubles the point for emphasis. al-wilāda and al-saʿāda rhyme.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا سَمِعَ الْمَلِكُ بِالْوَلَدِ فَرِحَ فَرَحًا جَلِيلًا وَأَعْطَى الْمُبَشِّرَ مَالًا جَزِيلًا وَمِنْ فَرْحَتِهِ تَوَجَّهَ إِلَى الْغُلَامِ وَقَبَّلَهُ بَيْنَ عَيْنَيْهِ وَتَعَجَّبَ مِنْ جَمَالِهِ الْبَاهِرِ وَتَحَقَّقَ فِيهِ قَوْلُ الشَّاعِرِ
sentences.tr: fa-lammā samiʿa al-maliku bi-al-waladi fariḥa faraḥan jalīlan wa-aʿṭā al-mubashshira mālan jazīlan wa-min farḥatihi tawajjaha ilā al-ghulāmi wa-qabbalahu bayna ʿaynayhi wa-taʿajjaba min jamālihi al-bāhiri wa-taḥaqqaqa fīhi qawlu al-shāʿiri
sentences.l: And when the king heard of the child, he rejoiced a rejoicing great, and gave the bringer-of-good-news wealth abundant; and from his joy he went to the boy and kissed him between his eyes, and marvelled at his beauty dazzling; and there came-true in him the saying of the poet:
sentences.i: When the king heard of the child he rejoiced greatly and gave the bearer of the good news a handsome reward. In his joy he went to the boy, kissed him between the eyes and marvelled at his dazzling beauty; and in him the poet's words came true:
sentences.n: samiʿa bi-, “hear of”, the verb choosing the preposition. jalīlan and jazīlan rhyme.

sentences.t:
اَللّٰهُ خَوَّلَ مِنْهُ آجَامَ الْعُلَا * اَسَدًا وَآفَاقُ الرَّآسَةَ كَوْكَبًا
هَشَّتْ لِمَطْلَعِهِ الْاَسِنَّةُ وَالْاَسِرَّةُ * وَالْمَحَافِلُ وَالْجَحَافِلُ وَالظُّبَى
لَاتَرْكَبُوهُ عَلَى النُّهُودِ فَاِنَّهُ * لَيَرَى ظُهُورَ الْخَيْلِ اَوْطَاءَ مَرْكَبَا
وَلْتَفْطِمُوهُ عَنِ الرَّضَاعِ فَاِنَّهُ * لَيَرَى دَمَ الْاَعْدَاءِ اَحْلَى مَشْرَبَا
sentences.tr:
allāhu khawwala minhu ājāma al-ʿulā * asadan wa-āfāqu al-raʾāsata kawkaban
hashshat li-maṭlaʿihi al-asinnatu wa-al-asirratu * wa-al-maḥāfilu wa-al-jaḥāfilu wa-al-ẓubā
lā tarkabūhu ʿalā al-nuhūdi fa-innahu * la-yarā ẓuhūra al-khayli awṭāʾa markabā
wa-l-tafṭimūhu ʿani al-raḍāʿi fa-innahu * la-yarā dama al-aʿdāʾi aḥlā mashrabā
sentences.l:
God has granted from him to the thickets of the heights a lion, and the horizons of the leadership a star.
At his rising rejoiced the spear-points and the thrones, and the assemblies and the hosts and the sword-edges.
Do not ride him on the breasts, for he surely sees the backs of the horses (as) the smoothest mount;
and wean him from the suckling, for he surely sees the blood of the enemies (as) the sweetest drink.
sentences.i:
God has given the thickets of glory a lion in him, and the horizons of command a star.
At his rising the spearheads were glad, and the thrones, the assemblies, the armies and the swords.
Do not carry him at the breast: he holds the backs of horses the softest seat.
Wean him from milk: he holds the blood of enemies the sweetest drink.
sentences.n: The verse is copied as the print points it. In the first line the print has wa-āfāqu, nominative, and al-raʾāsata, accusative, where the grammar wants wa-āfāqa al-raʾāsati, “and (has given) the horizons of leadership (a star)”; it is translated by that sense. raʾāsa is a by-form of riʾāsa, “headship, command”. In the third line the print points lā tarkabūhu, “do not ride him”; probably for lā turkibūhu (form IV), “do not set him riding”, that is, do not carry him on the bosom, and it is translated so. awṭāʾa is awṭaʾa, “smoothest, most comfortable”, printed with a long ā. wa-l-tafṭimūhu in the fourth line uses the lām of command with a second-person verb, a rare, poetic turn. The rhyme is on -bā.

sentences.t: ثُمَّ إِنَّ الدَّايَاتِ أَخَذْنَ ذَلِكَ الْمَوْلُودَ وَقَطَعْنَ سُرَّتَهُ وَكَحَّلْنَ مُقْلَتَهُ ثُمَّ سَمَّوْهُ تَاجَ الْمُلُوكِ خَارَانَ وَارْتَضَعَ ثَدْيَ الدَّلَالِ وَتَرَبَّى فِي حِجْرِ الْإِقْبَالِ
sentences.tr: thumma inna al-dāyāti akhadhna dhālika al-mawlūda wa-qaṭaʿna surratahu wa-kaḥḥalna muqlatahu thumma sammawhu tāja al-mulūki khārāna wa-irtaḍaʿa thadya al-dalāli wa-tarabbā fī ḥijri al-iqbāli
sentences.l: Then the midwives took that newborn and cut his navel and kohled his eye; then they named him Tāj al-Mulūk Khārān. And he sucked the breast of the indulgence and was-reared in the lap of the good-fortune,
sentences.i: The midwives took the newborn, cut his cord and lined his eyes with kohl, and he was named Tāj al-Mulūk Khārān. He was nursed at the breast of tenderness and brought up in the lap of good fortune,
sentences.n: dāya, “midwife, wet-nurse”, is a Persian loanword. Tāj al-Mulūk means “Crown of Kings”; Khārān is not explained. The midwives are feminine (akhadhna), but sammawhu, “they named him”, is masculine plural: people in general. al-dalāl and al-iqbāl rhyme: dalāl is fond indulgence, iqbāl the favour of fortune.

sentences.t: وَلَازَالَتِ الْأَيَّامُ تَجْرِى وَالْأَعْوَامُ تَمْضِي حَتَّى صَارَلَهُ مِنَ الْعُمْرِ سَبْعُ سِنِينَ
sentences.tr: wa-lā zālati al-ayyāmu tajrī wa-al-aʿwāmu tamḍī ḥattā ṣāra lahu mina al-ʿumri sabʿu sinīna
sentences.l: and the days did not cease running and the years passing, until there became to him of the age seven years.
sentences.i: and the days ran on and the years went by, until he was seven years old.
sentences.n: The print has ولازات, a misprint for ولازالت, “and (they) did not cease”, corrected here. lā zālat for narrative “did not cease” is a looser usage; Classical prose says mā zālat or lam tazal, and with lā the phrase usually expresses a wish. It sets صار له, “there became to him”, as one word, صارله.

sentences.t: فَعِنْدَ ذَلِكَ أَحْضَرَ الْمَلِكُ سُلَيْمَانُ شَاهْ الْعُلَمَاءَ وَالْحُكَمَاءَ وَأَمَرَهُمْ أَنْ يُعَلِّمُوا وَلَدَهُ الْخَطَّ وَالْحِكْمَةَ وَالْأَدَبَ فَمَكَثُوا عَلَى ذَلِكَ مُدَّةَ سِنِينَ حَتَّى تَعَلَّمَ مَا يَحْتَاجُ إِلَيْهِ الْأَمْرُ
sentences.tr: fa-ʿinda dhālika aḥḍara al-maliku sulaymānu shāh al-ʿulamāʾa wa-al-ḥukamāʾa wa-amarahum an yuʿallimū waladahu al-khaṭṭa wa-al-ḥikmata wa-al-adaba fa-makathū ʿalā dhālika muddata sinīna ḥattā taʿallama mā yaḥtāju ilayhi al-amru
sentences.l: And at that, King Sulaymān Shāh summoned the learned and the sages and ordered them that they teach his son the script and the wisdom and the refinement; and they stayed at that a period of years, until he learned what the matter needs.
sentences.i: Then King Sulaymān Shāh summoned the scholars and the sages and ordered them to teach his son penmanship, philosophy and polite letters. They kept at it for some years, until he had learned all that his station required.
sentences.n: al-khaṭṭ is handwriting, the art of the pen; adab is the whole of courtly culture — letters, manners and eloquence.

sentences.t: فَلَمَّا عَرَفَ جَمِيعَ مَا طَلَبَهُ الْمَلِكُ أَحْضَرَهُ مِنْ عِنْدِ الْفُقَهَاءِ وَالْمُعَلِّمِينَ وَأَحْضَرَ لَهُ أُسْتَاذًا يُعَلِّمُهُ الْفُرُوسِيَّةَ فَلَمْ يَزَلْ يُعَلِّمُهُ حَتَّى صَارَ لَهُ مِنَ الْعُمْرِ أَرْبَعَةَ عَشَرَ سَنَةً
sentences.tr: fa-lammā ʿarafa jamīʿa mā ṭalabahu al-maliku aḥḍarahu min ʿindi al-fuqahāʾi wa-al-muʿallimīna wa-aḥḍara lahu ustādhan yuʿallimuhu al-furūsiyyata fa-lam yazal yuʿallimuhu ḥattā ṣāra lahu mina al-ʿumri arbaʿata ʿashara sanatan
sentences.l: And when he knew all that the king had sought, he (the king) fetched him from the presence of the jurists and the teachers, and fetched for him a master to teach him the horsemanship; and he did not cease teaching him until there became to him of the age fourteen years.
sentences.i: When the boy had mastered everything the king required, the king took him away from the jurists and teachers and brought in a master to train him in horsemanship, who went on teaching him until he was fourteen years old.
sentences.n: arbaʿata ʿashara sanatan, “fourteen years”, uses the masculine numeral with the feminine sana, where Classical Arabic has arbaʿa ʿashrata sanatan; the vocalisation follows the text. The subject changes without warning from the boy (“he knew”) to the king (“he fetched him”).

sentences.t: وَكَانَ إِذَا خَرَجَ إِلَى بَعْضِ أَشْغَالِهِ يَفْتَتِنُ بِهِ كُلُّ مَنْ رَآهُ
sentences.tr: wa-kāna idhā kharaja ilā baʿḍi ashghālihi yaftatinu bihi kullu man raʾāhu
sentences.l: And he was — when he went-out to some of his affairs, there was-enchanted by him everyone who saw him.
sentences.i: And whenever he went out on any business of his, everyone who saw him was captivated.
sentences.n: iftatana bi-, “be enchanted by, be infatuated with”, the verb choosing the preposition.

sentences.t: وَأَدْرَكَ شَهْرَزَادَ الصَّبَاحُ فَسَكَتَتْ عَنِ الْكَلَامِ الْمُبَاحِ
sentences.tr: wa-adraka shahrazāda al-ṣabāḥu fa-sakatat ʿani al-kalāmi al-mubāḥi
sentences.l: And the morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent from the permitted speech.
sentences.i: Morning overtook Shahrazād, and she fell silent, leaving the permitted speech.
